name: Intel

Software Engineer (new grad/campus).dsaDepth: Moderate — an OA for freshers, then 1-3 technical rounds mixing coding with genuinely deep OS/CS-fundamentals and C/C++ pointer/memory questions, plus real project-defense pressure
rounds: Online assessment (new grads/interns): 60-90 min, ~2 problems, easy-medium (arrays, strings, basic logic) — experienced hires often skip straight to the recruiter
Recruiter/HR phone screen (~30-45 min): background, motivation, salary expectations

Technical screen/interview(s) (45-110 min each, 1-3 rounds): live coding (arrays, linked lists, recursion, bit manipulation, trees) in C/C++/Python/Java, PLUS a strong emphasis on OS, computer organization, caching, synchronization, pointers/memory management, DBMS, Linux, networking and OOP — genuinely deep for a "software" role given Intel’s hardware-adjacent culture
Project defense: interviewers push hard for specifics (dataset sources, preprocessing choices, architecture decisions, exact project timeline), not just bullet-point summaries
Closing manager round (~30 min): fit and career direction
extraTopics: Real depth on OS/computer-organization/memory topics, not just DSA — this shows up repeatedly and is more emphasized than at typical product companies
Defending project specifics in detail: dataset choices, why a particular database or architecture was picked, exact timelines
C/C++ pointer and bit-manipulation fluency, reflecting Intel’s hardware-adjacent software culture
Software Engineer (new grad/campus).notes: India campus drives (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune) typically run all rounds in a single day; off-campus candidates get an extra 40-60 min phone/virtual technical screen first. Software (CSE/IT) and hardware (ECE/EEE) tracks are interviewed differently.
